issues.body: The round-1 defect is still present. On byte 10 (i == 9), payload.checked_shl(63) returns Some for payloads greater than 1 because the shift amount itself is valid; overflowing high bits are discarded. Thus a terminal tenth byte such as 0x02 can be accepted and normalized to a smaller u64, contradicting the documented rejection of over-64-bit values and the fail-closed lookup_multihash contract. No new test exercises this overflow boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Reject i == 9 when payload > 1 before combining it (or use checked arithmetic that detects value overflow). Add coverage for the maximal valid u64 varint and invalid tenth-byte payloads such as 0x02 and 0x7f, including a lookup_multihash or parse_multihash assertion proving the public path rejects them.
issues.title: Ten-byte varints still overflow u64 and decode as another value

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: the prior major fail-closed varint overflow remains unchanged. read_varint still uses checked_shl, which validates the shift count but does not detect significant payload bits discarded when the tenth byte is shifted by 63. The added tests still cover truncation and non-minimal encoding only, so malformed greater-than-u64 multihashes may be accepted as a different value.
